references.text: Jesus' actions of washing the disciples' feet after taking off his clothes, followed by teaching that the disciples should do the same, are directly connected to the action in verse 4 where he rises, takes off his clothes, and wraps a towel around himself.
The verse describes the immediate continuation of the action in verse 4, where Jesus, having wrapped himself with the towel, pours water into a basin and washes the disciples' feet.
The context for the action in verse 4 is that Jesus, knowing his time had come to leave the world, rose from the meal to perform this act of love and service.
Jesus refers to his own action in verses 4–5 as an example of service, where he, as Lord and Teacher, has washed the disciples' feet, and commands them to do likewise.
Jesus draws a direct parallel between his action in verses 4–5 (a servant is not greater than his master) and the expectation that the disciples should perform similar acts of service.
